arxiv-2012-12640.title: Gradient-Free Adversarial Attacks for Bayesian Neural Networks
arxiv-2012-12640.creator: Matthew Yuan, Matthew Wicker, Luca Laurenti
arxiv-2012-12640.description: Abstract The existence of adversarial examples, i.e., small perturbations to their inputs that can cause a misclassification, underscores the importance of understanding the robustness of machine learning models. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs), due to their calibrated uncertainty, have been shown to posses favorable adversarial robustness properties.

arxiv-2109-08989.title: Passive Optical Networking for 5G and Beyond 5G Low-Latency Mobile Fronthauling Services
arxiv-2109-08989.creator: Oscar J. Ciceri, Carlos A. Astudillo, Gustavo B. Figueiredo, Zuqing Zhu, and Nelson L. S. da Fonseca
arxiv-2109-08989.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Oscar J. Ciceri, Carlos A. Astudillo, Gustavo B. Figueiredo, Zuqing Zhu, and Nelson L. S. da Fonseca. Passive optical network (PON) technology offers an attractive cost-efficient alternative to support 5G and Beyond 5G mobile network fronthauling (MFH). However, MFH for such networks is challenging given its high bandwidth and strict latency requirements.

arxiv-2209-10994.title: The Arecibo Galaxy Environment Survey XII : Optically dark HI clouds in the Leo I Group
arxiv-2209-10994.creator: Rhys Taylor, Joachim Köppen, Pavel Jáchym, Robert Minchin, Jan Palouš, Jessica L. Rosenberg, Stephen Schneider, Richard Wünsch, Boris Deshev
arxiv-2209-10994.description: Abstract Using data from the Arecibo Galaxy Environment Survey, we report the discovery of five H i clouds in the Leo I group without detected optical counterparts. Three of the clouds are found midway between M96 and M95, one is only 10 ′ from the south-east side of the well-known Leo Ring, and the fifth is relatively isolated.

arxiv-2211-02002.title: Emergence of Competing Orders and Possible Quantum Spin Liquid in SU(N) Fermions
arxiv-2211-02002.creator: Xue-Jia Yu, Shao-Hang Shi, Limei Xu, Zi-Xiang Li
arxiv-2211-02002.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xue-Jia Yu, Shao-Hang Shi, Limei Xu, Zi-Xiang Li. In the past decades, tremendous efforts have been made towards understanding the exotic physics emerging from competition between various ordering tendencies in strongly correlated systems. Employing state-of-the-art quantum Monte-Carlo simulation, we investigate an interacting SU( N N ) fermionic model with varying interaction strength and value of N N , and unveil the ground-state phase diagram of the model exhibiting a plethora of exotic phases.

arxiv-2212-07338.title: Studies of the muon momentum calibration and performance of the ATLAS detector with p ​ p pp collisions at s \sqrt{s} =13 TeV
arxiv-2212-07338.description: Abstract This paper presents the muon momentum calibration and performance studies for the ATLAS detector based on the p ​ p pp collisions data sample produced at s \sqrt{s} = 13 TeV at the LHC during Run 2 and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb − 1 \mathrm{fb^{-1}} .

arxiv-2301-10124.title: Dynamics of blood cells during a routine laboratory examination
arxiv-2301-10124.creator: Mesfin Asfaw Taye
arxiv-2301-10124.description: Abstract Abstract Centrifugation is a commonly performed laboratory procedure that helps to separate blood cells such as R ​ B ​ C ​ s RBCs , W ​ B ​ C ​ s WBCs , and platelets from plasma or serum.

arxiv-2303-04804.title: Time optimal quantum state transfer in a fully-connected quantum computer
arxiv-2303-04804.creator: Casey Jameson, Bora Basyildiz, Daniel Moore, Kyle Clark, Zhexuan Gong
arxiv-2303-04804.description: Abstract The speed limit of quantum state transfer (QST) in a system of interacting particles is not only important for quantum information processing, but also directly linked to Lieb-Robinson-type bounds that are crucial for understanding various aspects of quantum many-body physics. For strongly long-range interacting systems such as a fully-connected quantum computer, such a speed limit is still unknown.

arxiv-2307-13026.title: Precision tracking of massive black hole spin evolution with LISA
arxiv-2307-13026.creator: Geraint Pratten, Patricia Schmidt, Hannah Middleton, Alberto Vecchio
arxiv-2307-13026.description: Abstract The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will play a vital role in constraining the origin and evolution of massive black holes throughout the Universe. In this study we use a waveform model (IMRPhenomXPHM) that includes both precession and higher multipoles, and full Bayesian inference to explore the accuracy to which LISA can constrain the binary parameters.

arxiv-2502-01202.title: Noether Symmetries in f ⁡ ( Q ) − f\left(Q\right)- Cosmology
arxiv-2502-01202.creator: Konstantinos F. Dialektopoulos, Genly Leon, Andronikos Paliathanasis
arxiv-2502-01202.description: Abstract We apply the Noether symmetry analysis in f ⁡ ( Q ) f\left(Q\right) -Cosmology to determine invariant functions and conservation laws for the cosmological field equations. For the FLRW background and the four families of connections, it is found that only power-law f ⁡ ( Q ) f\left(Q\right) functions admit point Noether symmetries.

arxiv-2502-17151.title: Dynamics near a class of nonhyperbolic fixed points
arxiv-2502-17151.creator: Meihua Jin, Shihao Meng, Yunhua Zhou
arxiv-2502-17151.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate some dynamical properties near a nonhyperbolic fixed point. Under some conditions on the higher nonlinear terms, we establish a stable manifold theorem and a degenerate Hartman theorem. Furthermore, the finite shadowing property also be discussed.

arxiv-2510-15963.title: ESCA : Contextualizing Embodied Agents via Scene-Graph Generation
arxiv-2510-15963.creator: Jiani HuangUniversity of Pennsylvania jianih@seas.upenn.edu, Amish Sethi University of Pennsylvania asethi04@seas.upenn.edu, Matthew Kuo University of Pennsylvania mkuo@seas.upenn.edu Mayank KeoliyaUniversity of Pennsylvania mkeoliya@seas.upenn.edu Neelay VelingkerUniversity of Pennsylvania neelay@s
arxiv-2510-15963.description: Abstract Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) are making rapid progress toward general-purpose embodied agents. However, existing MLLMs do not reliably capture fine-grained links between low-level visual features and high-level textual semantics, leading to weak grounding and inaccurate perception. To overcome this challenge, we propose ESCA , a framework that contextualizes embodied agents by grounding their perception in spatial-temporal scene graphs.

arxiv-2602-02455.title: Drift-Bench : D iagnosing Coope R ative Breakdowns in LLM Agents under I nput F aults via Multi- T urn Interaction
arxiv-2602-02455.creator: Han Bao, Zheyuan Zhang, Pengcheng Jing, Zhengqing Yuan, Kaiwen Shi, Yanfang Ye
arxiv-2602-02455.description: Abstract As Large Language Models transition to autonomous agents, user inputs frequently violate cooperative assumptions (e.g., implicit intent, missing parameters, false presuppositions, or ambiguous expressions), creating execution risks that text-only evaluations do not capture. Existing benchmarks typically assume well-specified instructions or restrict evaluation to text-only, single-turn clarification, and thus do not measure multi-turn disambiguation under grounded execution risk.

pmc-10524812.title: Clinical Informatics in Critical Care Medicine
pmc-10524812.creator: Girish N. Nadkarni, Ankit Sakhuja
pmc-10524812.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Continuous monitoring and treatment of patients in intensive care units generates vast amounts of data. Critical Care Medicine clinicians incorporate this continuously evolving data to make split-second, life or death decisions for management of these patients. Despite the abundance of data, it can be challenging to consider every accessible data point when making the quick decisions necessary at the point of care. Consequently, Clinical Informatics offers a natural partnership to improve the care for critically ill patients.

pmc-10609809.title: Exploring Cholinergic Compounds for Peripheral Neuropathic Pain Management: A Comprehensive Scoping Review of Rodent Model Studies
pmc-10609809.creator: Edouard Montigné, David Balayssac, Sergio Marques Borghi
pmc-10609809.description: Neuropathic pain affects about 7–8% of the population, and its management still poses challenges with unmet needs. Over the past decades, researchers have explored the cholinergic system (muscarinic and nicotinic acetylcholine receptors: mAChR and nAChR) and compounds targeting these receptors as potential analgesics for neuropathic pain management.

pmc-11481460.title: Recombinant Lactococcus lactis secreting FliC protein nanobodies for resistance against Salmonella enteritidis invasion in the intestinal tract
pmc-11481460.creator: Ming Yang, Kui Gu, Qiang Xu, Renqiao Wen, Jinpeng Li, Changyu Zhou, Yu Zhao, Miwan Shi, Yuan Weng, Boyan Guo, Changwei Lei, Yong Sun, Hongning Wang
pmc-11481460.description: Salmonella Enteritidis is a major foodborne pathogen throughout the world and the increase in antibiotic resistance of Salmonella poses a significant threat to public safety. Natural nanobodies exhibit high affinity, thermal stability, ease of production, and notably higher diversity, making them widely applicable for the treatment of viral and bacterial infections.

pmc-11567922.title: ZEB2 drives intra-tumor heterogeneity and skin squamous cell carcinoma formation with distinct EMP transition states
pmc-11567922.creator: Jeroen Verstappe, Nicolas Skrypek, Jordy De Coninck, Bieke Soen, Joachim Taminau, Marianthi Tatari, Kenneth Bruneel, Nele Loret, Kato De Clercq, Caroline Van den Broecke, Koen Van De Vijver, Jo Van Dorpe, Jody Haigh, Bram De Craene, Steven Goossens, Niels Vandamme, Geert Berx
pmc-11567922.description: SummaryAbout 5% of patients with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) have a poor prognosis which is associated with a loss of tumor differentiation, invasion and metastasis, all of which are linked to the process of epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity (EMP). Here, we showed that the EMP-associated transcription factor ZEB2 drives cSCC heterogeneity which resembles biphasic carcinosarcoma-like tumors.

pmc-11646892.title: Improving Diagnosis and Management of Dilated Cardiomyopathy With Advanced Cardiac Imaging and Early Genetic Testing
pmc-11646892.creator: Karen Flores Rosario, Melissa A Daubert
pmc-11646892.description: Corresponding AuthorKey Words: cardiac magnetic resonance, cardiomyopathy, genetic testing, positron emission tomography The multiple etiologies for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) can make diagnosis and treatment extremely challenging. Furthermore, optimal evidence-based management may be delayed if the underlying pathobiology is not initially identified. Over one-third of DCM cases have a genetic cause or result from a genetic predisposition.

pmc-12565905.title: Shear Performance Degradation of Fiber-Reinforced Recycled Aggregate Concrete Beams Under Salt Freeze–Thaw Cycles
pmc-12565905.creator: Shefeng Guo, Jin Wu, Jingmiao Zhao, Zhehong Zeng, Xiangyu Wang, Yiyuan Wang, Haoxiang Luan, Yulin Wang, Dongxia Hu
pmc-12565905.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In saline soil and alpine regions of northwest China, fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete (FR-RAC) beams are subjected to coupled degradation from a chloride–sulfate composite salt attack and freeze–thaw cycling. Existing studies predominantly focus on natural aggregate concrete in freshwater environments or single-salt solutions, with limited documentation on the shear performance of FR-RAC beams after freeze–thaw exposure in chloride–sulfate composite salt solutions.

pmc-13326503.title: Membrane‐type I metalloproteinase (MT1‐MMP): A key modifier of extracellular matrix microenvironment
pmc-13326503.creator: Yoshifumi Itoh, Masaki Inada
pmc-13326503.description: Extracellular matrix (ECM) is a major component of the cellular microenvironment. It holds cells, directly sends signals to the cells, pools growth factors and cytokines, and guides cell migration and differentiation. A type I transmembrane proteinase, membrane‐type I matrix metalloproteinase (MT1‐MMP/MMP14), degrades ECM at the cell surface and cleaves cell surface receptors, thereby modifying cellular behavior.

pmc-13406496.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Treatment Response to Vitamin D3 in Adolescents and Young Adults with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Prospective, Open-Label, Alternation-Based Comparative Study
pmc-13406496.creator: Marina Adriana Mercioni, Adrian Goldiș, Nina Holban, Mihai Vasile Popescu, Radu Dragomir, Christian Goldiș, Bianca Belei, Ileana Enatescu, Roxana Folescu, Laura Olariu, Oana Belei
pmc-13406496.description: Background: Chronic inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), specifically Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis, present substantial clinical challenges characterized by a relapsing-remitting course. These conditions often lead to serious complications and significantly impair nutritional status, physical development, and overall quality of life. Methods: This unicentric, prospective, open-label, alternation-based comparative study investigated the efficacy of vitamin D3 supplementation in adolescents with IBD.

pmc-13474880.creator: Chava Kurtz, Odelia Ben Harush, Anna Zisberg, Paola Buedo, Stuart McLennan, Efrat Shadmi
pmc-13474880.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite global efforts to promote equitable healthy ageing, substantial gaps remain.
